title: Partnerships and channels
description: Review how resellers, integrators, technology partners and marketplaces sell, deploy or extend the product, and what the partner agreement allows.
expertises: Partner programme design, tiers and incentives
questions: Who sells, deploys or supports the product in this change: us, a partner or both?
What does the partner agreement allow on pricing, territory, branding and customer data?
How will partners learn about the change and who answers their questions?

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/720, Vertical Block Exemption Regulation
European Commission, Vertical block exemptions and Guidelines on vertical restraints
IFRS Foundation, IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

specialists.title: Partner programme manager
specialists.focus: Define the partner tiers, entry criteria, benefits and obligations the change touches, and check that each tier can be measured.
checks: Each tier has written entry criteria and the data that proves them, such as certified staff or sourced revenue.
Benefits and obligations are the same for every partner of a tier, or the exception is recorded.
The programme names who reviews tier status and how often.

specialists.title: Channel economics analyst
specialists.focus: Check the margin, discount and referral fee each partner type receives and whether the deal still makes money for both sides.
checks: Partner discounts and fees are compared with the direct price on the same scope and term.
Revenue presentation is checked with finance: whether the company acts as principal or agent changes revenue under IFRS 15.
Channel conflict rules say who owns a deal when a partner and the direct team meet the same customer.

specialists.title: Partner agreement specialist
specialists.focus: Compare the change with the reseller, referral or marketplace agreement: territory, resale price, branding, customer data and termination.
checks: The agreement does not fix or impose a minimum resale price: under Regulation (EU) 2022/720 that removes the block exemption.
Territory or customer restrictions are checked with legal against the hardcore restrictions of the vertical rules.
Who is controller or processor of end-customer data is written in the agreement.

specialists.title: Partner enablement and technical alliances lead
specialists.focus: Plan the training, certification, sandbox and integration documentation partners need before they sell or deploy the change.
checks: Partners get release information before end customers, with a date.
Integration partners have a test environment and the deprecation calendar of the APIs they use.
Marketplace listings are updated with the same claims as the product documentation.

evidence: Current partner agreements or programme guide for the partner types involved.
Price list, partner discount grid and referral fees, with their effective dates.
Partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline or revenue for the segment concerned.
Partner enablement material, certification requirements and integration documentation.
challenge: Would the change put partners in competition with our own sales team on the same customers?
Does any clause or practice fix the price a reseller charges or restrict where it sells?
What happens to customers and their data when a partner leaves the programme?
Is a partner the right route, or would a direct offer or an integration serve the customer better?
decision_criteria: Proceed when partner terms, economics and enablement are defined and legal has checked the restrictions.
Revise when partner margins or fees make the deal unprofitable for either side at the expected volume.
Block when a term would fix resale prices or impose a restriction legal classifies as hardcore, until it is removed.
Name the partner metric, such as sourced pipeline or certified partners, and the review date.
